<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/knowledge-turso`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **84** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/LICENSE`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/README.md`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/package.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**26** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a89a01239b31e735e4754ad8c45be9e898c82e18`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/LICENSE`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/README.md`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/package.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `VALIDATION_ERROR (literal, 38 pages)`, `organization_id (literal, 42 pages)`
- **27** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a89a01239b31e735e4754ad8c45be9e898c82e18` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8a7e8ce3f67657b18cad9a2292eaaca89f70a797` — the merge of head `f073750af7c4b688d3ecc8be57a13c75766c97ac` into base `a89a01239b31e735e4754ad8c45be9e898c82e18`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8a7e8ce3f67657b18cad9a2292eaaca89f70a797 && git checkout 8a7e8ce3f67657b18cad9a2292eaaca89f70a797
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a89a01239b31e735e4754ad8c45be9e898c82e18 f073750af7c4b688d3ecc8be57a13c75766c97ac && git checkout -B drift-repro a89a01239b31e735e4754ad8c45be9e898c82e18 && git merge --no-ff f073750af7c4b688d3ecc8be57a13c75766c97ac

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a89a01239b31e735e4754ad8c45be9e898c82e18
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a89a01239b31e735e4754ad8c45be9e898c82e18` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:cloud#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbW5anP6GDaVi5LKi2U

## 维护者速读

- 这个 PR 把原来放在 cloud 仓库的 libSQL 向量库搬进开源框架：本地开发和不用 PostgreSQL 的部署，可以把向量存在自己的一个 knowledge.db 文件里。
- 复核结论：暂不通过，退回开发补一轮。主要问题一处：识别"旧版本留下的表"的规则太宽。知识源如果恰好取了某一个合法名字，第一次完整重建索引就会删掉这个库自己的登记表，之后所有知识源都无法检索，重启后索引要全部重建；与别的表共用一个数据库时，同名规律的无关表也会被删。本机已复现。
- 审核期间 PR 更新过一次：合并了主干，并补上了"限定范围检索"。这部分复核没有问题，范围过滤在数据库里、排序之前执行，查不到的方向只会少返回，不会多返回。
- 另有三处应改：连接远程 libSQL 没有超时；两条从 pgvector 那轮定下的约定没有测试钉住；文档有两句话和现状不符，PR 正文的数字也还停在旧版本。
- 自动检查还在跑（36 项未完成），目前没有失败项。
- 需要您做的：无。cloud 仓库删除旧包仍是另一张 cloud 卡，要点列在下面"范围外去向"。

## 席位核对

REWORK — M1 is open at this head: the rule that recognises a table of the package's earlier releases is too wide, and a complete reindex can drop a table that is not one, the store's own generation table included. S1 to S3 stand beside it. The merge of `main` and the record scope, owed since #37342 landed, are in this head and hold.

Head-sha: `9c469ddf28f8f1c0aab5e3b8e74d736550285c06`

Read in two parts. First the PR at `56f3dc5e2b10819f33ec24cd19c81d19b987dec9` (4 commits, 23 files, +2331 / -37). Then the delta, no force push: `68654e1d` merges `main` at `db77cc49`, and `9c469ddf` adds the record scope (8 files of the PR's own: the adapter, `sql.ts`, two test files, the README, the changeset, two docs pages). The PR against `main` at this head: 23 files, +2390 / -37, the same 23 paths as before.

**形态**
- Open, draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #37107`, the only closing keyword in the body. `Fixes` is right: every numbered item of the card is delivered; removing the package from the cloud repo is the card's own out-of-scope line.
- Body and changeset read `Clause-②: yes` · `Metadata-protocol: none`. The changeset names `@objectstack/knowledge-turso`, `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/service-settings` at `patch`; the new package joins the fixed group in `.changeset/config.json`.
- Not governed surface: `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 37388` reads 0 of 23 paths on the register, 2427 changed lines, under the 3000 threshold. No `.github/workflows` path.
- Every path is inside the claim as amended twice (comment 7177625794): the ledger row, and the Turso hint with its header list and test. The ledger's generated mirror lists codes only and does not change. `packages/spec/llms.txt` (77 to 78 packages) is the generated package count a gate demands.
- `LICENSE` is the Apache-2.0 text, byte for byte the root `LICENSE` and the one of `knowledge-pgvector`; `package.json` says `Apache-2.0`.
- `mergeable_state` is `blocked`.

**门禁 check-runs** (at `9c469ddf`, read 2026-11-26)
- 22 success, 9 skipped, 36 in progress, 0 failed. Lint · repo & tooling gates and the other Lint jobs read success, bar PM dispatch-gates and Lint UI, still running. Type Check · source gates success; workspace, consumer gates, debt ledger and UI not measured. Test Core, all ten shards, and Test UI, all sixteen: not measured. Build Core, Build Docs: not measured. All-green: not measured.
- Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL) is an expected skip on the PR.
- Local at `9c469ddf` in a scratch worktree: `knowledge-turso` vitest 125/125 (3 files; the dev reports 124), `typecheck` with `check:test-typecheck` exit 0. Local at `56f3dc5e`: 103/103, as the dev reports.

**对照 knowledge-pgvector 的约定** (#37337)
1. Coded refusals carry a `remedy`; driver text only there — holds. `KNOWLEDGE_REBUILD_REQUIRED` and both `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` shapes have one-sentence messages; the load failure, the open failure and the file name travel in `remedy`. The no-embedder refusal has no `remedy`, as in the reference.
2. Embedder resolved before any fingerprint compare — holds on `search` and on `listDocuments`. Pinned on `search` (1 red when moved); not pinned on `listDocuments` (fix 3).
3. A first generation never adopts leftover rows — holds in code (the table is made afresh); not pinned (fix 3).
4. `docHash` and `headingPath` on hits — holds; 4 red when left off.
5. Organization filter before ranking — holds, in the inner `WHERE`; 4 red when dropped.
6. Chunk-hash skip — holds; 2 red when removed.
7. No cached kernel embedder — holds; a getter read at each call, pinned.
8. A connection timeout — holds for a file (the busy timeout); absent for a remote URL (fix 2).
9. No raw driver text to `search_knowledge` callers — holds. A libSQL error carries no `status`, so the service reads it as uncoded and logs it.

**逐项核对与消融** (21 single-change ablations in a scratch worktree, each restored; worktree removed)
1. Generations — `beginBuild` opens a table beside the active one, takes up a build of the same fingerprint, drops one of another; `completeBuild` switches inside one transaction. The switch made at `beginBuild` instead: 4 red. The fingerprint compare removed from `search`: 4 red.
2. Legacy table — refused on search (2 red when removed), dropped at `completeBuild` (2 red when kept). The recognition rule is too wide: fix 1.
3. One builder per source — the unique index holds one generation under construction per source. It does not refuse a second builder: a second `beginBuild` under the same fingerprint joins the build, and under another fingerprint replaces it, after which the first builder's writes are refused 409. No mixed generation results either way. Probed locally. Accepted as a deviation from the words of K7 rule 3, which the contract gives an adapter no way to meet (no builder identity); the prose is fix 4.
4. The in-process queue — holds; made pass-through, the concurrency case is red with `TRANSACTION_ACTIVE` and `SQLITE_BUSY`. Embed calls run outside it.
5. SQL — table names come from a source id held to the whitelist and an integer, and the mapping from source and generation to a name is one to one. Every value is a bound parameter: organization ids, scope ids, field names, filter keys and values, cursors, document ids. Whitelist removed: 2 red.
6. Tenant isolation — the organization filter is on the one ranked read; a search reads the active generation only, and one under construction is never ranked. `listDocuments` and `delete` are service-side and take no caller filter, as in the reference.
7. The platform-file refusal — holds by name and by `OS_DATABASE_URL`; 2 red when removed. It reads spellings, not files: fix 5.
8. Secrets — the auth token is handed to the client only. Four malformed URLs carrying a credential were tried: no warning, `remedy` or health message echoed it.
9. Degrading — a failed `@libsql/client` load registers an unavailable adapter; rethrown, 1 red.
10. Record scope (delta) — an empty scope answers nothing before any query; terms are a union inside the inner `WHERE` beside the organization filter; ids and the field name are bound; hits carry the document's metadata. Scope `WHERE` dropped: 14 red. Early return removed: 2 red. Union made an intersection: 2 red.
11. Record scope, numbers (delta) — 19 stored numbers probed against the service's `String(value)`. Whole numbers and short decimals match. Seven do not (exponent forms, more than 15 significant digits): each is a miss in SQL. Where SQL's text is shorter than the service's, the service's check after the answer drops the hit. Fewer hits, never more: fix 6.
12. Merge (delta) — one conflict, the adapter table row of `knowledge.mdx`; both rows kept. No file of this PR outside the eight changes between the two heads.

**逐句核的散文面**
- Changeset: every bullet read against the code. True, except "One builder per source, held by a unique index" (fix 4).
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx` §4.2, the diagram, the contract paragraph, the example, the status row: true as written; the scope clause matches the code.
- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`: "so `os dev` on SQLite gets semantic search … with nothing to install" is not true today: the package is added and the plugin registered by hand until #37102 (fix 4). The rest is true.
- README: true, except the same builder sentence.
- `knowledge.manifest.ts` hint and header: true today. Nothing mounts the store from settings until #37102; "registered beside the knowledge service, with this URL" says so, and the no-URL text names the plugin's own default file.
- PR body: stale at this head. It says 103 cases and "whichever lands second owes the other's suite cases", and its local-runs block is pinned to `56f3dc5e` (fix 4).

**修复清单**
1. M1 · 必须修 — the earlier-release table is recognised by one missing column alone, so a table that is not one can be taken for one and dropped by a complete reindex; the store's generation table is reachable this way through a legal source id. Recognise it by its own shape, keep the generation table out by name, and pin both. Reproduced locally at both heads; the steps are in the seat's reply, not here.
2. S1 · 应修 — no bound on a call to a remote database. Boot awaits the health check, and one stalled request holds the queue of every source on that client. Bound it, as the reference does with its connection timeout.
3. S2 · 应修 — two conventions of the reference are not pinned: a first generation made afresh (the DROP removed: 125 green), and `listDocuments` with no embedder answering 503 and not 409 (the order changed: 125 green).
4. S3 · 应修，散文面 — prose: "nothing to install"; "one builder per source" in the changeset, README, `knowledge.mdx` and TSDoc, which should say what the index holds; the PR body re-pinned to this head.
5. nit — the platform-file refusal compares spellings: an encoded or differently cased name, and a database named by a flag or a bare path, are not caught. A foot-gun guard for an operator's own option, not a boundary.
6. nit — scope and filter numbers in exponent form or past 15 digits are in no scope on this adapter; in one shape the service then logs that the adapter does not apply the scope.
7. nit — a source id the spec allows but longer than 48 characters is refused uncoded; SQLite has no such limit.
8. nit — not pinned: the generation recheck inside the write transaction, and the scalar-type guard of a scope term (each removed: 125 green). The third-attempt write error names a made-up passage id; the search retry on a switched generation has no bound.

**接受的偏差**
- No DiskANN index and so no `vector_top_k` on the CI runner (card item 6): the exact scan is what K8 item 9 needs, and `vector32` runs in the test shards.
- A second builder joins or replaces rather than being refused (point 3 above).
- Two processes writing one file are covered by the busy timeout's `PRAGMA` pin, not by a two-process case.

**范围外去向**
- cloud: `packages/knowledge-turso` there has the same name at 6.9.0 and is still publishable. Version numbers do not collide (6.x against this repo's track), and nothing in cloud imports it outside its own directory. The cloud card: remove the package, or mark it `private` first, before any cloud release that would publish it, so the `latest` tag is not moved back to a 6.x build whose `LICENSE` file is the other text; take its name out of the four pending changesets that bump it; update `docs/design/package-publish-posture.md`, ADR-0119's line on when it leaves, `scripts/lint-baseline.json` and the acknowledgement notes that cite its path. Whether the 6.x releases are deprecated on npm is the maintainer's. Which workflow published 6.9.0: not measured.
- #37102: the mount names the store's path; a `file:` URL taken from settings must be held to the data directory there.
- #37104: rewrites the manifest whose hint this PR only corrects.

**落地条款**
- Clause-② declared and the path limb hit; the contract record below is FAIL at this head. The PR stays draft. A patch round to the same dev: M1 with its tests, then S1 to S3. A head that moves past prose owes a fresh record; every check at the landing head green or an expected skip before the queue.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9c469ddf28f8f1c0aab5e3b8e74d736550285c06`
Local-runs: probe — the package suite at both heads, 21 single-change ablations, and probes of the legacy rule, the builder lock, the store URL and the scope's number reading were run in a scratch worktree to confirm what the diff reads as; nothing was pushed.
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts + packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/turso-adapter.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/sql.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/plugin.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/__tests__/contract.test.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/__tests__/acceptance.test.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/package.json
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: yes

### ① Derived judgments

- The diff adds no contract member. It is the reader K8 item 16 names: items 1, 5, 7, 8 and 9 and nothing past them, with the generation table and lock row inside the adapter (K7 rule 2). The delta adds the reader of item 17 as the dated note of 2026-11-25 shapes it.
- The one published-schema line is the ledger row for `@objectstack/knowledge-turso`, the same code and status the row of `knowledge-pgvector` registers. Its comment says the code also covers a source whose only index is an earlier-release table; the adapter does throw it there.
- K7 rules 1, 4 and 5 hold: a write goes to the generation of the fingerprint it carries or is refused; a search under another fingerprint than the active one's is refused and never answered from it; no query ranks two generations.
- K7 rule 3 holds in part: a build is opened only by `beginBuild`, and an unfinished one is resumed or replaced. "Refuses a second builder" is not met and cannot be with what the contract carries; recorded as an accepted deviation by the seat.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes`, `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. A new published package widens the public surface; no metadata key changes.
- `patch` for all three packages is what the fixed group and the no-major gate take. The package name is published at 6.9.0 from another repository, and the changeset lists the exports and options removed against those releases, which is where a consumer of them reads the break.
- `@objectstack/spec` at `patch`: one additive ledger row and a package count.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flags and `open_questions`: none open. The four out-of-scope carriers are answered in the seat section.
- SQL push-down: the organization filter, the record scope and the metadata filter are in the ranking statement; no id is materialised in the application. The direction Prime Directive 5 asks for. No finding.
- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
- Overlap: #37342 is in the base at this head, and the suite's `implements.scope` is declared `true`.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`
- Holds. One row, additive, the code already registered for the sibling store; the comment is true of the adapter.

`packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/turso-adapter.ts`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/sql.ts`
- The refusal the ledger row registers is thrown with code, status 409, a one-sentence message and a `remedy`, on a write and on a search, and the acceptance cases assert code and status.
- The earlier-release path does not hold as designed.

M1 (must-fix) — the rule that recognises an earlier-release table is too wide: a table that is not one is refused as one and then dropped by a complete reindex, the store's own generation table among them. After that every source of the store fails until a restart and is then rebuilt from nothing. It is reachable through a source id the spec allows. Reproduced at both heads.

- The record scope agrees with the term type and with the reference's reading: a record term on the stored record id, a metadata term on a stored string or number as text or any such element of a list, anything else matching nothing, an empty scope ranking nothing.

`packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/plugin.ts`
- The store never opens the platform's file by default, and the refusal of a named platform file holds for the spellings the docs list. The plugin registers an unavailable adapter instead of failing the boot.

S1 (should-fix) — a call to a remote database has no bound, while boot awaits the health check and one queue serves every source of the client.

`packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/__tests__/contract.test.ts`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/__tests__/acceptance.test.ts`
- Every member of the suite is declared and runs on both stores, with no service image.

S2 (should-fix) — two conventions of the reference are held in code and pinned by no case: the first generation made afresh, and `listDocuments` with no embedder.

`packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/package.json`
- Hold. The exports are the adapter, the plugin, the two names #37102 reads and the table-name helpers; one entry point, Apache-2.0, `files` ships `dist` and the README.

Implemented-by: `session_01JQwxbaMuehXzctoWq7iRsV`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbW5anP6GDaVi5LKi2U`

**VERDICT: FAIL**
